clue.text: The bosun is out to make extra money

indicators.note: something out of place is disordered, so the letters of bosun are rearranged

explanation.surface: A ship's bosun goes ashore to earn a little more on the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is out' signals that the five letters of BOSUN are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonus is a payment over and above normal wages.

clue.text: Strict clergyman turns up in the diocese

indicators.note: the clergyman sits inside the word for the diocese

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the clergyman's word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a clergyman

explanation.surface: A stern vicar makes an appearance within the bishop's territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reverses REV to VER, and 'in' places VER inside SEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe and strict are synonyms describing harsh, uncompromising discipline.

clue.text: Animal disinfectant mixed deep inside the vessel

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are placed within the word for vessel

parts.note: a ship is a sea-going vessel

indicators.note: mixed up means the letters of deep are rearranged

explanation.surface: A farm chemical has been blended at the bottom of a container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' turns DEEP into EEPD, and 'inside' puts that within SHIP.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheep dip is the insecticidal wash in which flocks are dunked to kill parasites.

clue.text: A stroke by a batsman, going for a run perhaps?

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a shot driven to the leg side, in front of the wicket
read as two words: out for a spin in the car

explanation.walkthrough: Cricket is a bat-and-ball game; a 'run' is a cricket score but here also a car trip.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, a drive struck to the leg side is so named, and someone heading out for a spin in the car is literally out motoring.

clue.text: Makings of a mountain?

parts.note: the idiom about exaggeration: something small is what one makes a mountain out of

explanation.walkthrough: The clue points at the idiom for exaggerating a trivial problem.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying 'make a mountain out of a ...' names the little mound of earth a burrowing mammal throws up.

clue.text: One tap-bar drunk may think himself Napoleon

indicators.note: a drunk is confused, so the letters of one tap-bar are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone who has had too much at the bar fancies himself a French emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges the nine letters ONETAPBAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The French emperor's family surname, the classic delusion of a deranged person.

clue.text: Skeleton service?

parts.note: read as a set of crockery made from what a skeleton is made of

explanation.walkthrough: 'Skeleton service' suggests a minimal staff; a 'service' is also a set of tableware.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine porcelain made with ash of animal skeletons, sold as dinner services.

clue.text: Test for car or engine

parts.note: the MOT is the annual British roadworthiness test for cars
taken as written

explanation.surface: A garage offers either a vehicle inspection or a check on the engine.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is the UK's yearly compulsory vehicle safety test, named after the old Ministry of Transport.
explanation.definitionFit: A motor is a machine that drives something, an engine.

clue.text: Time to do a hand's turn

definitions.text: Time to do a hand's turn

parts.words: Time to do a hand's turn
parts.note: the period the minute hand of a clock takes to go once round the dial

explanation.walkthrough: 'a hand's turn' sounds like a spell of work, but it is a clock hand going round.
explanation.definitionFit: Sixty minutes is the period a clock's minute hand needs to sweep once round the face.

clue.text: A train driver

parts.note: read as one who drives a train of pack animals rather than a railway engine

explanation.walkthrough: 'train' suggests the railway; a mule train is a line of pack animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A muleteer drives a string of mules, and such a string is called a train.

clue.text: No traffic is met in such a street

definitions.text: No traffic is met in such a street

parts.words: No traffic is met in such a street
parts.note: vehicles all travel the same direction, so none comes towards you

explanation.walkthrough: 'met' means coming the other way: all vehicles here go the same direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A street where vehicles may travel in only one direction has no oncoming traffic.

clue.text: Go ahead with a new deal

indicators.note: a new version of the word deal is its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone pushes on to the front with a fresh business agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges DEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To go ahead is to be in front, at the head of the field.

clue.text: Musical instrument untouched

definitions.meaning: a small keyboard instrument of the harpsichord family, popular in Tudor times

explanation.definitionFit: Both a small Tudor harpsichord and an adjective meaning pristine or chaste share the spelling.

clue.text: Responding to a phone call about disturbing news

indicators.note: the article and phone call go around the jumbled letters

parts.note: a ring is a telephone call

indicators.note: to disturb something is to mix it up, so the letters of news are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone takes a call reporting upsetting news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbing' turns NEWS into NSWE, and 'about' places A and RING around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Answering and responding both mean replying to someone.

clue.text: Rough-looking punk met with violence

indicators.note: violently treated, the letters of punk met are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A scruffy punk got into a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with violence' rearranges PUNKMET.
explanation.definitionFit: Unkempt describes untidy, scruffy hair or appearance.

clue.text: Emergency exit for a pilot

parts.note: a fighter pilot leaves a stricken plane by being shot out in the seat

explanation.definitionFit: A pilot in trouble is propelled clear of the cockpit by a rocket-powered seat.

clue.text: Cut off, and also tie off

indicators.note: off means wrong or out of order, so the letters of also tie are rearranged

explanation.surface: A surgeon severs a vessel and ties it off too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges ALSOTIE. 'Cut off' looks like part of a surgical instruction but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To isolate something is to separate it from everything around it.

clue.text: There's a certain wildness in such devious dealings

indicators.note: a certain wildness in the letters signals that the word wildness is jumbled

explanation.surface: Crooked business carries an air of untamed recklessness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'There's a certain' points to a degree of disorder in the letters WILDNESS, which rearrange into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Swindles are frauds, crooked schemes that cheat people of money.

clue.text: Dash to get article into cheap production

indicators.note: the article goes inside the rearranged letters
a production reworks material, so the letters of cheap are rearranged

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A dash to get a news article into an inexpensive show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'production' turns CHEAP into PACHE; 'into' places AN inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Dash and panache both mean stylish flair and verve.

clue.text: Toothsome vegetable-grown only for decoration

parts.note: toothsome means tasty, sweet
a pea is a green vegetable

explanation.surface: A tasty vegetable grown purely for show.
explanation.walkthrough: Unlike the garden pea, the sweet pea is a climbing flower, and its pods are not eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: The fragrant climbing plant is cultivated for its blooms, not as a food crop.

clue.text: Wolves forwards playing Rugby

definitions.meaning: a group of wolves hunting together
the eight forwards in a rugby union scrum

explanation.walkthrough: 'Wolves' suggests Wolverhampton Wanderers, an English football club, but here it means the animals.
explanation.definitionFit: The collective noun for wolves also names a rugby team's scrummaging forwards.

clue.text: Trendy accountant was found in Peru

parts.note: in means fashionable
CA, chartered accountant

explanation.surface: A fashionable financier turned up in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: CA stands for Chartered Accountant. 'was found in Peru' defines one of the people of the old Andean empire.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the ancient people who ruled an empire in Peru before the Spanish conquest.

clue.text: Stick around at home like a dog

indicators.note: the stick goes around the word for at home

parts.note: a cane is a walking stick
in means at home

explanation.surface: Fetching a stick and staying in the house like a pet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' wraps CANE around IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Canine is the adjective for dogs, as feline is for cats.

clue.text: Finish with conclusion of judge in lawsuit

indicators.note: the last letter of judge sits inside the word for lawsuit

parts.note: a case is a lawsuit

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A trial ends when the judge sums up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conclusion of' gives E from 'judge', and 'in' puts it inside CASE.
explanation.definitionFit: To cease is to stop or bring to an end.

clue.text: Pole position?

parts.note: read as the region around the North Pole, not the front of a motor-racing grid

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole position' is the motor-racing term for the front of the starting grid.
explanation.definitionFit: The polar region surrounding the North Pole is where that pole is located.

clue.text: Highly attractive part of Belgium

parts.note: a hilly, wooded and scenic region in the south-east of that country

explanation.walkthrough: 'Highly' hints at hills: the region is upland, as well as very attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: A forested upland region of southern Belgium famed for its scenery.

clue.text: Vegetable has one on both sides

indicators.note: the two copies stand at either side of the letter for one
both means the word on is used twice

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A vegetable with one placed on each side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'both' doubles ON, and 'sides' puts I between the two.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulb with layers, used in cooking as a vegetable.

clue.text: Port of fine quality

definitions.meaning: a town and harbour on the Isle of Sheppey in Kent
the quality of being sheer, very thin and fine like delicate fabric

explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A Kent harbour town shares its name with the state of being diaphanous, as fabric can be.
